problem_type: fake success / false-positive connection state: saving a vendor API key could leave the vendor row enabled while the credential landed disabled-pending-certification, so the model-settings home listed the vendor under '已接入 / N 个可使用' even though resolveTextBrainKeys (which requires an enabled credential) returned null — a green 'connected' state that generation could not use
symptom: In an isolated profile, writing an APIMart key through the renderer credential path WITHOUT the paired vendor de-publish (a bare modelCatalog.upsertVendorApiKey, e.g. the shape the apimart-text-brain e2e uses) left vendor.enabled=true and hasApiKey=true, while the credential record was enabled:false (renderer sanitizer forces this — certification owns the enabled transition). projectOnboardingConnections then put the vendor in connectedKnown (filter hasApiKey && enabled) and ModelSettingsHome rendered it under '已接入 / N 个可使用'. But resolveTextBrainKeys → resolveConfiguredTextBrain requires configuredCredential(record) = record.enabled && enc==='safeStorage' && apiKey.trim(); with the credential disabled it returned null, so the text brain and every generation reported 'no usable text model'. Real-machine four-path probe: A (real UI save, which pairs upsertVendor({enabled:false})) → available section, resolver null (consistent); B (certified terminal) → connected + resolver brain (consistent); C (UI-saved terminal, vendor+cred disabled) → available, resolver null (consistent); D (bare credential write, vendor left enabled) → '已接入 / 28 个可使用' BUT resolver null (INCONSISTENT). D is the reported gap.
direct_cause: upsertRendererCatalogVendorApiKey wrote the credential disabled-pending-certification but did not touch the vendor's enabled flag. The 'shown as connected ⟺ actually usable' invariant was therefore upheld only by convention: the three UI components that save keys (KnownVendorKeyConnectPage, VendorOnboardCard, CustomVendorManage) each ALSO call upsertVendor({enabled:false}) right before the credential write. Any caller that writes a credential without that manual pairing (a bare bridge/MCP call, the e2e harness, or a future fourth UI path) leaves vendor.enabled=true beside a disabled credential, which the home projection reads as connected/usable while the resolver reads as unusable.
class_root: Connected/usable state for a vendor must be derived from a single source of truth, not from two flags (vendor.enabled and credential.enabled) that separate call sites are trusted to keep in sync. A renderer credential edit is always disabled-pending-certification and always invalidates any prior certification, so it must de-publish the vendor in the SAME operation at the one shared boundary every renderer credential save funnels through — rather than each UI caller remembering the paired upsertVendor({enabled:false}). Enforcing it per-card invites each new save path to skip the pairing and re-introduce the desync.
affected_population: Every vendor whose API key is written through the renderer credential path without an accompanying vendor de-publish: it must not be listed as 已接入 / N 个可使用 while its credential is disabled-pending-certification and resolveTextBrainKeys cannot use it

Every future save path or connector that writes a vendor credential: it inherits the obligation that a disabled-pending-certification credential leaves the vendor out of the connected/executable projection, enforced at the shared boundary rather than re-implemented per caller
entry_points: applyApiKeyUpsert (electron/catalog/catalogStore.ts) — the innermost boundary EVERY credential write funnels through: the renderer IPC path (upsertModelCatalogVendorApiKey), package import (importModelCatalogPackage), and every main-process mutateCatalog writer (serviceCatalog register/stage, catalogCommit, integrationSession, customCallDraft) plus tikhubConnectorService. When the credential lands enabled===false it calls depublishVendorForDisabledCredential on the same in-memory state, so the de-publish rides the caller's single writeCatalog — a disabled-pending-certification credential can never coexist with an enabled vendor, and there is no intermediate on-disk state in which it could

upsertRendererCatalogVendorApiKey (electron/catalog/rendererCatalogMutation.ts) — the renderer credential-save choke point (IPC nomi:model-catalog:vendor-api-key:upsert). It sanitizes the credential to enabled:false and delegates; the paired vendor de-publish is inherited from applyApiKeyUpsert rather than re-implemented here

resolveTextBrainKeys / configuredCredential (electron/ai/textBrainResolver.ts) — the read-side 'is this usable' authority: requires the credential record.enabled && enc==='safeStorage' && apiKey.trim(); a disabled credential yields null. This is the truth the UI must agree with

projectOnboardingConnections (src/ui/onboarding/onboardingDrawerConnections.ts) — connectedKnown = knownCards.filter(hasApiKey && enabled); once the boundary keeps vendor.enabled=false for a disabled credential, a vendor pending certification stays in availableKnown (the 可接入 section) instead of 已接入
internal_only_reason: This is an internal state-consistency fix between two Nomi-owned catalog flags (vendor.enabled and credential.enabled) and the Nomi-owned resolver/home projection; no third-party API contract governs it. The authoritative design it aligns with is the ratified internal plan docs/plan/2026-08-30-unified-model-integration-certification.md (models stay uncertified until certification promotes them; no migration may convert an uncertified mode into enabled; only live-certified may be described as verified). De-publishing the vendor on a renderer credential edit — which invalidates any prior certification — is the correct fail-closed effect, and the next canonical certification run re-promotes it. Verified against the real Nomi build via an isolated-profile four-path probe, not against any external service.
invariants: ANY credential write that lands enabled===false de-publishes its vendor in the same store operation: applyApiKeyUpsert calls depublishVendorForDisabledCredential on the same in-memory CatalogState the caller will writeCatalog once, so vendor.enabled=true can never coexist with a disabled-pending-certification credential — regardless of which caller (renderer IPC, package import, or any main-process mutateCatalog writer) performed the write, and with no window on disk where the two disagree.

The model-settings home lists a vendor under 已接入 / N 个可使用 only when resolveTextBrainKeys can actually use it: because connectedKnown gates on vendor.enabled and the store keeps an uncertified vendor disabled, the home 'connected' state and the resolver's 'usable' verdict agree (verified across the bare-credential and certified terminal states).

Certification's promote family needs no exemption flag: the guard's trigger IS 'the credential landed enabled===false'. Every promote/registration/connector write passes enabled:true (serviceCatalog register/stage, catalogCommit, integrationSession, customCallDraft, tikhubConnectorService), so they are excluded by construction. Adding a skip option would be an escape hatch (P1) and the exact thing a future caller would get wrong.

The guard only rewrites an ENABLED vendor, so an already-disabled staging vendor is not rewritten on every key edit (no needless updatedAt churn); and it flips only enabled+updatedAt in place rather than re-deriving the row through applyVendorUpsert, so vendor name/meta/connection-scope fields survive a credential edit untouched.
generality_proof: The de-publish is enforced at the innermost boundary all credential writes share, not per UI card and not per process side. Every renderer credential save (KnownVendorKeyConnectPage, VendorOnboardCard, CustomVendorManage, any future or bare bridge/MCP caller) funnels through IPC → upsertRendererCatalogVendorApiKey → upsertModelCatalogVendorApiKey → applyApiKeyUpsert; package import reaches the same function via importModelCatalogPackage; and every main-process writer reaches it via mutateCatalog's tx.upsertApiKey. Because the invariant sits at that convergence point and mutates the same in-memory state the caller commits once, it is inherited rather than re-implemented, and it holds atomically (the earlier renderer-level version issued two separate writeCatalog calls, leaving a crash window in between). The three UI components' pre-existing manual upsertVendor({enabled:false}) calls remain redundant defense-in-depth (locked by manualCertificationBoundary.test.ts). The read-side authority (configuredCredential in textBrainResolver.ts) and the home projection (connectedKnown in onboardingDrawerConnections.ts) are each single-sourced, so 'usable' and 'shown connected' are both derived from vendor.enabled + credential.enabled in exactly one place each; the store keeps those two flags consistent by construction.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Owns the 'a disabled credential de-publishes its vendor' invariant plus its rationale. A pure in-place CatalogState edit (flips only enabled+updatedAt on an enabled vendor) so it can ride whichever writeCatalog its caller performs.

The innermost boundary every credential write shares — renderer IPC, package import, and all main-process mutateCatalog writers. It applies the invariant to the same in-memory state the caller commits once, so no credential writer, present or future, can leave an enabled vendor beside a disabled credential and surface a 已接入/N 个可使用 vendor that resolveTextBrainKeys cannot use.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: applyApiKeyUpsert de-publish-on-disabled-credential (inherited by upsertModelCatalogVendorApiKey, importModelCatalogPackage, and mutateCatalog's tx.upsertApiKey)
same_class_entry_points.evidence: credentialPublication.test.ts drives the real store over a temp userData dir and asserts, per writer family: single write (renderer IPC path), mutateCatalog transaction (the main-process family), and package import all persist vendor.enabled=false alongside a disabled credential, re-read from disk to prove it is one commit rather than an in-memory coincidence; a companion case pins that name/meta/baseUrlHint/providerKind/createdAt survive the de-publish. Positive control run: removing the single guard line turns exactly those 4 inheritance cases red while the promote-family cases stay green.

rendererCatalogMutation.test.ts asserts the boundary forces the credential to enabled:false and issues NO second vendor write of its own, so the de-publish is inherited from the store rather than duplicated here (P1: no parallel implementation). Real-machine walkthrough credential-connect-honesty.walk.mjs pins that after a bare upsertVendorApiKey the vendor.enabled=false, apimart is NOT in the 已接入 section, and resolveTextBrain is null (consistent).

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: register/stage tx.upsertApiKey({...enabled:true}) — the certification registration + staging credential writes
same_class_entry_points.evidence: All three write sites (register x2, stage) pass enabled:true, so the enabled===false trigger excludes them by construction — no exemption flag exists or is needed. credentialPublication.test.ts pins the promote shape (tx.upsertVendor({enabled:true}) then tx.upsertApiKey({enabled:true})) still ends enabled, and that an omitted enabled defaults to true. Full electron/providerAdapter + electron/integrationCertification suites pass unchanged.

The connector only persists a credential after its verification call succeeds, and writes enabled:true, so the guard never fires for it. tikhubConnectorService.test.ts asserts the exact call shape ({apiKey:'good-key', enabled:true}) and that failed verification writes nothing; it passes unchanged.

Manual onboarding commits the user's key as enabled:true inside the same mutateCatalog transaction that writes vendor+model+mapping, so the guard's enabled===false trigger excludes it. The electron/catalog suite (112 files, 1303 tests) passes unchanged with the guard in place.

The home projection already gates the connected section on vendor.enabled; it needed no change. With the boundary keeping an uncertified vendor disabled, an unusable vendor stays in availableKnown. credential-connect-honesty.walk.mjs asserts the connected-section membership equals resolver usability for both the bare-credential and certified terminal states.

textBrainResolver.test.ts already pins that a disabled credential is treated as missing (resolveTextBrainStatus === missing, chooseTextModel throws no-usable-text-model) without touching the keychain. This is the read-side truth the UI is now made to agree with; it is unchanged by this fix.

prevention.invariant: A vendor whose credential is written disabled-pending-certification — by ANY writer — is de-published within the same store operation, so vendor.enabled=true cannot coexist with a disabled credential, and the home '已接入 / N 个可使用' state cannot be shown for a vendor resolveTextBrainKeys cannot use.
prevention.failure_mode: Enforced only at the renderer boundary, the invariant covered one of several credential writers: any main-process writer (a new connector, a certification repair path, an import) that persisted a disabled credential while leaving the vendor enabled re-opened the '已接入 but unusable' fake success. The renderer-level version was also two separate writeCatalog calls, so a crash between them left exactly the desync it existed to prevent.
prevention.strategy: Push the de-publish down to applyApiKeyUpsert — the innermost boundary every credential write shares — so it applies to the same in-memory state the caller commits in one writeCatalog. Trigger on the written credential being enabled===false, which excludes the promote/registration/connector family (all write enabled:true) by construction instead of by an exemption flag. The renderer boundary keeps only its sanitizer and delegates, so there is no second implementation to drift.

recurrence.reason: Deriving a vendor's connected/usable state from two flags (vendor.enabled + credential.enabled) that separate call sites keep in sync is a recurring desync class. Rather than trusting each save path to pair the vendor de-publish, the de-publish is enforced at the one renderer credential-save boundary, and the read-side usability and the home projection are each single-sourced, so a future save path inherits the guarantee.
same_class_scan: Enumerated every renderer credential-save entry point (grep upsertVendorApiKey across src/ + electron/): the three UI components (KnownVendorKeyConnectPage, VendorOnboardCard, CustomVendorManage) all funnel through modelCatalog.upsertVendorApiKey → IPC nomi:model-catalog:vendor-api-key:upsert → upsertRendererCatalogVendorApiKey. All three ALSO call upsertVendor({enabled:false}) manually; those become redundant belt-and-suspenders after the boundary fix and are kept + locked by manualCertificationBoundary.test.ts. No renderer save path bypasses the boundary.

Checked the MCP integration path: nomi_integration_open_credentials opens the secure Nomi credentials page and never receives or echoes keys (electron/capabilityCore/mcpIntegrationTools.ts), so the MCP agent cannot write a bare credential; the only bare-credential writers are the e2e harness and any direct bridge call, which the boundary now guards.

Confirmed certification's promote path is main-process (ProviderAdapterService.commitPromotion / integrationCertification) and does NOT go through upsertRendererCatalogVendorApiKey. Real-machine certified terminal state (walkthrough state ②) shows vendor.enabled=true + resolver brain + 已接入, unaffected.

Second pass (2026-09-01): enumerated every MAIN-PROCESS credential writer by grepping applyApiKeyUpsert / upsertApiKey / upsertModelCatalogVendorApiKey across electron/. Six write sites — serviceCatalog.ts register (x2) and stage, catalogCommit.ts, integrationSession.ts, customCallDraft.ts — all reach applyApiKeyUpsert via mutateCatalog and all pass enabled:true; tikhubConnectorService.ts calls upsertModelCatalogVendorApiKey with enabled:true after verification. The one main-process path whose credential enabled comes from untrusted data is importModelCatalogPackage (catalogStore.ts, apiKey taken from the package payload) — it now inherits the guard, which is the correct effect since a package pairing a disabled credential with an enabled vendor is precisely the desync. No live bug existed at any of these sites; the invariant is now structural rather than conventional.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed from rendererCatalogMutation.ts: the renderer-level de-publish (the second upsertModelCatalogVendor write inside upsertRendererCatalogVendorApiKey) and its vendorIsPublished helper, deleted in the same commit that moves the invariant into applyApiKeyUpsert (P1: no parallel version, no fallback). When the invariant moved down, the renderer-level copy was deleted rather than left as belt-and-suspenders: keeping it would mean two implementations of the same rule that can drift, and its round-trip through sanitizeRendererVendorMutation/applyVendorUpsert re-derived the whole vendor row (reducing meta to {adapter}) where the store-level version flips only enabled+updatedAt. The three UI components' manual upsertVendor({enabled:false}) calls are a different thing and are intentionally kept — they set the vendor's own publication state on the save path and are asserted by manualCertificationBoundary.test.ts, not a competing implementation of the credential-driven de-publish.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency is added, upgraded, or retained. The fix is a same-operation catalog write through the existing store functions.

migration: No stored data is rewritten and no schema changes. Existing catalogs are unaffected at rest: a vendor that is already enabled with a usable (safeStorage, enabled) credential — i.e. certification-promoted — is never touched by this path unless the user re-edits the credential, in which case de-publishing is the correct effect (a credential edit invalidates the prior certification and the next canonical run re-promotes). A vendor left in the desynced state by a prior bare credential write self-heals the next time its credential is written through the boundary.
residual_risks: CLOSED (2026-09-01, second pass): the de-publish previously covered only the RENDERER credential-save boundary, leaving any future main-process writer to re-open the desync. It now lives in applyApiKeyUpsert, the innermost boundary all credential writes share, so main-process writers inherit it; the promote family is excluded by the enabled===false trigger rather than by an exemption. Remaining sliver: within a single mutateCatalog transaction a caller could write a disabled credential and then explicitly tx.upsertVendor({enabled:true}) afterwards, and last-write-wins would re-publish. No current caller does this (all six main-process write sites pass enabled:true), and the reverse order fails closed; the ordering rule is documented in credentialPublication.ts.

The connected/usable agreement is proven for the text-brain resolver (the reported failure). Media models publish through a different path (adapter modes / mappings); their per-node usability is gated by modelHasPublishedExecution, but the same vendor.enabled gate governs whether the vendor appears in the connected section, so a disabled vendor cannot show any kind as 已接入.

The walkthrough's certified terminal state is constructed by seeding a safeStorage credential via the real bridge then flipping enabled flags on disk; it faithfully reproduces the post-promote flag combination but does not run the full paid certification pipeline (covered separately). The bare-credential state IS driven entirely through the real bridge path the fix guards.
